scope: Fixed development photos, no ROI, supplied corners or label masks. Three arms: production; frozen held-out network body/material fields; the same body plus RGB-palette illumination correction. All use the same twenty-two full photographs. No additional training. This follows the palette development experiment; it is not an untouched test set. Crop support/geometry checks unchanged. Derived-mask template agreement is NOT source-artwork accuracy.
methodOrder: Rotate the declared order by source index; same ten-second fitting allowance, no per-image candidate selection across arms.
conclusions: Color calibration improves known paper-region classification but does not increase checked reconstruction count: RGB and uncorrected network each produce 3/22 versus production 7/22.
Both learned-field arms fail 19/22 times before fitting. The updated colors cannot compensate for incomplete or contaminated body fields and unsupported crop hypotheses.
RGB gains the candle at 0.36625% disagreement with its own derived mask, while losing the rabbit crop that the uncorrected field supports. These are different outputs, not a uniform improvement.
The RGB checker masks retain much sharper cell corners than the network, but small gaps and border distortions remain. The candle silhouette and frame are visibly recognizable.
Production reconstructs the newly annotated fish at 1.116875% derived-mask disagreement; the neural arms fail its crop despite the RGB field recovering its interior colors.

The bicycle remains a solver/representation failure after a usable production crop: the returned weave loses the bicycle despite a clear classified target. More accurate body fields alone will not solve this case.
limitations: All are repeatedly inspected development photographs; none is a newly untouched generalization test.
Derived masks and crops differ by arm. Their percentages cannot be compared as errors against one shared original artwork.
No original cutting paths, dense boundary topology labels or physical assembly checks.
The RGB correction uses 256-pixel letterboxed predictions; native-photo boundary reconstruction remains untested.
This evaluates single selected candidates from each arm, not a deployed combined fallback policy.
